claim: Anthropic released Opus 5.5 with lower reported task cost, stronger long-horizon coding performance, external pre-release evaluation and action-level safeguards.
verifiedFacts: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5 on September 22.
Anthropic reports 40% lower typical running cost than Opus 5 and more than 30% faster output.
Anthropic says the model was externally tested by Frontier Design and METR before release.
Anthropic describes an action classifier, auditable sandbox and pre-merge code review for agentic coding.
Early testers reported long unattended and multi-repository engineering tasks, though those reports are vendor-selected.
inference: As long-horizon agents become cheaper and more capable, governance cost shifts from supervising every step to defining authority, checkpoints, evidence and integration conditions before execution.

Consultancy implication: bounded handoff design and receipt quality become more valuable as agent sessions grow longer. Project disposition: Seed Loom CORE; no model-specific architecture change is justified.
significance: High: improved economics make unattended multi-step work more plausible, increasing the practical value of governed delegation and integration receipts.
assumptions: Vendor and early-tester results are directionally representative of real workloads.
knownLimitations: Most performance and safety evidence is provider-produced or provider-selected.
Benchmark superiority does not guarantee better results on Jennipher's repositories.
